title.en: Armed man arrested near Trump's golf course ahead of president's visit
title.zh: 武装男子在特朗普高尔夫球场附近被捕，此前总统将到访

summary.en: An armed man was arrested near President Trump's golf course shortly before the president was scheduled to host a fundraising dinner there.
summary.zh: 一名持枪男子在特朗普总统的高尔夫球场附近被捕，此前不久，特朗普总统原定在那里主持一场筹款晚宴。

body.en:
Authorities in California have arrested a man who was seen near a golf course owned by President Donald Trump in the Los Angeles area, just ahead of the president's visit for a fundraising dinner there.

Jeanine John Taele, 38, was found with a pistol and armour-piercing ammunition in his vehicle at the Trump National Golf Course in Rancho Palos Verdes, investigators say.

According to the Los Angeles Sheriff's Department, he was "observed walking throughout the golf course grounds taking photographs and videos and appearing to monitor security-planning activities".

The arrest took place on Sunday afternoon. Trump is currently visiting California to attend a Republican party fundraising dinner.

In a news release, the sheriff's department said Taele was arrested after plainclothes federal agents reported a suspicious person to local authorities.

When police confronted the man, they discovered that he was being sought in connection to a robbery by the El Segundo Police Department, about 15 miles (25km) north of Rancho Palos Verdes, a wealthy coastal enclave known for its hills and scenic cliffs.

Authorities searched him and found he was carrying a 16-round magazine containing hollow point ammunition. In his vehicle, which was parked at the golf course, they found a loaded pistol, along with a loaded magazine containing hallow-point ammunition.

Due to the "potential security implications surrounding the incident", officials obtained a warrant to search Taele's home and found an "illegally modified AR platform rifle" a .45 pistol, body armour, high-capacity magazines, a plethora of bullets for pistols and rifles and multiple notebooks "containing concerning statements".

"During the detention, deputies recovered a 16-round magazine containing hollow point ammunition from Taele's pants pocket," the statement says.

"Deputies subsequently searched Taele's vehicle and recovered a loaded pistol with a round chambered, along with an additional loaded magazine containing hollow point ammunition."

He was arrested for carrying a concealed firearm, and possession of armour-piercing or prohibited ammunition.

This breaking news story is being updated and more details will be published shortly. Please refresh the page for the fullest version.

You can receive Breaking News on a smartphone or tablet via the BBC News App . You can also follow @BBCBreaking on X , external to get the latest alerts.
body.zh: 加州当局逮捕了一名男子，该男子被发现在洛杉矶地区唐纳德·特朗普总统拥有的高尔夫球场附近，当时总统正前往那里参加筹款晚宴。 调查人员称，38 岁的珍妮·约翰·泰勒 (Jeanine John Taele) 在帕洛斯维迪斯牧场的特朗普国家高尔夫球场被发现车内藏有手枪和穿甲弹。 据洛杉矶治安部门称，他“被发现在高尔夫球场走来走去，拍摄照片和视频，并且似乎在监视安全规划活动”。 逮捕发生在周日下午。特朗普目前正在加利福尼亚州参加共和党筹款晚宴。 治安部门在一份新闻稿中表示，便衣联邦特工向地方当局报告了一名可疑人员后，泰勒被捕。 当警察与这名男子对峙时，发现他正在被埃尔塞贡多警察局通缉，该警察局位于兰乔帕洛斯维迪斯以北约 15 英里（25 公里）处，这是一个富裕的沿海飞地，以其山丘和风景优美的悬崖而闻名。 当局对他进行搜身，发现他携带了一本装有空心弹药的 16 发弹匣。在他停在高尔夫球场的车里，他们发现了一把上膛的手枪，以及一个装有空心弹药的弹匣。 由于“围绕该事件的潜在安全影响”，官员们获得了搜查Taele家的搜查令，并发现了一把“非法改装的AR平台步枪”、一支0.45手枪、防弹衣、大容量弹匣、大量手枪和步枪的子弹以及多本“包含有关声明”的笔记本。 声明称：“在拘留期间，警员从塔埃勒的裤子口袋里找到了一本 16 发弹匣，里面装有空心弹药。” “警员随后搜查了塔埃勒的车辆，发现了一把装有子弹的手枪，以及一个装有空心弹药的弹匣。” 他因携带隐藏枪支、持有穿甲弹或违禁弹药而被捕。 此突发新闻报道正在更新，更多详细信息将很快发布。请刷新页面以获得完整版本。 您可以通过 BBC 新闻应用程序在智能手机或平板电脑上接收突发新闻。您还可以在外部 X 上关注 @BBCBreaking 以获取最新警报。

reflection.en: The arrest of an armed individual near a public event reminds us of the constant vigilance needed to maintain peace and order. Yahweh's word warns that those who live by violence often fall by it, highlighting the destructive cycle that weapons can unleash. This incident, though contained, underscores the importance of preventing such cycles from ever...
reflection.zh: 在公共活动附近逮捕一名持枪男子，提醒我们维持和平与秩序需要持续的警惕。雅伟的话语警告说，那些靠暴力生活的人往往会因暴力而灭亡，这突显了武器可能释放的破坏性循环。尽管这次事件得到了控制，但它强调了阻止此类循环开始的重要性。

verse.textEn: All who draw the sword will die by the sword.
verse.textZh: 凡动刀的，必死在刀下。

title.en: Australia news live: Pocock says falling house prices a ‘good thing for our country’; Labor expands solar discount to commercial buildings
title.zh: 澳大利亚新闻直播：波科克称房价下跌“对我们国家是好事”；工党将太阳能折扣扩大到商业建筑

summary.en: A politician in Australia has stated that falling house prices are beneficial for the country, even as most homeowners continue to sell their properties for a profit. This comes as the Labor government expands solar discounts to commercial buildings.
summary.zh: 澳大利亚一位政治家表示，房价下跌对国家有利，尽管大多数房主仍在出售房产时获利。与此同时，工党政府将太阳能折扣扩大到商业建筑。

body.en:
Independent senator David Pocock said a housing correction “would be a good thing for our country”, adding house prices cannot grow at the rate they have over the past two decades.

It’s kind of just become this normal thing that house prices go up at a rapid rate. I think we’ve got to ask the question – what is housing for?

Housing is so fundamental to functioning as a human, to flourishing families, communities – we have to actually ensure that we can keep house prices in check over the next couple of decades while wages rise to get back to a point where housing is affordable in this country.

Pocock said it was great news that Labor had released a change to negative gearing laws to better protect widows and divorcees and drop the so-called “widow tax”.
body.zh: 独立参议员戴维·波科克表示，住房市场调整“对我们国家来说是一件好事”，并补充说房价不可能以过去二十年的速度增长。 房价快速上涨已经成为常态。我认为我们必须问一个问题——住房是用来做什么的？ 住房对于人类的正常运转、繁荣的家庭、社区至关重要——我们必须切实确保在未来几十年内控制房价，同时工资上涨，回到这个国家可以负担得起住房的水平。 波科克表示，工党发布了对负扣税法的修改，以更好地保护寡妇和离婚者，并取消所谓的“寡妇税”，这是个好消息。

reflection.en: This news highlights the tension between individual financial gain and the broader economic health of a nation. Yahweh's words remind us that our ultimate loyalties are tested when personal prosperity conflicts with the common good. It prompts us to consider what truly benefits our communities and where our deepest devotion lies.
reflection.zh: 这则新闻突显了个人经济利益与国家整体经济健康之间的张力。雅伟的话语提醒我们，当个人财富与公共利益发生冲突时，我们最终的忠诚会受到考验。它促使我们思考什么真正有益于我们的社区，以及我们最深切的忠诚所在。

verse.textEn: No one can serve two masters... You cannot serve both God and Mammon.

title.en: ‘Did you send that report?’ The Icac bombshell that came late for Damien Tudehope
title.zh: “你发那份报告了吗？” 独立反腐委员会迟来的重磅炸弹，让达米安·图德霍普措手不及

summary.en: Australia's Independent Commission Against Corruption (Icac) questioned former Liberal finance minister Damien Tudehope regarding a report, with a significant revelation emerging late in the proceedings.

reflection.en: Public office carries a sacred trust, and accountability bodies like Icac remind us that leadership is established through righteousness, not through hidden reports or delayed disclosures. Yahweh's word affirms that leaders who detest wrongdoing uphold the very foundation of their authority, fostering trust and stability within a nation.
reflection.zh: 公职承载着神圣的信任，而像独立反腐委员会这样的问责机构提醒我们，领导力是建立在公义之上，而非通过隐瞒报告或延迟披露。雅伟的话语肯定，厌恶作恶的领袖才能维护其权力的根基，从而在一个国家中培养信任和稳定。

verse.textEn: Kings detest wrongdoing, for a throne is established through righteousness.
verse.textZh: 作恶为王所憎恶，因国位是靠公义坚立。

title.en: SpaceX beats revenue expectations in first earnings report after IPO crash
title.zh: SpaceX在首次公开募股股价下跌后，首份财报营收超预期

summary.en: SpaceX announced its first earnings report since going public, revealing $7.81 billion in revenue, a 92% increase, despite an initial share price crash. This report provides the public with a look into the financial performance of the trillion-dollar corporation.
summary.zh: SpaceX公布了其上市以来的首份财报，显示营收达到78.1亿美元，增长92%，尽管此前首次公开募股后股价曾下跌。这份报告首次向公众展示了这家万亿美元公司的财务状况。

body.en: Company posts $7.81bn in revenue, a jump of 92%, after share prices crashed following IPO debut For the first time since SpaceX went public, the world is getting a first-hand look into the trillion-dollar corporation’s financials. The Elon Musk -run business reported its second-quarter earnings on Tuesday, saying that its revenue jumped 92% since June. SpaceX beat Wall Street expectations, reporting $7.81bn in revenue, versus analysts’ predictions of $6.93bn. While expansive, the company is not profitable. The company reported a loss of $541m, down from a $1bn loss in the same quarter last year. Continue reading...
body.zh: 在 IPO 后股价暴跌后，该公司实现收入 78.1 亿美元，猛增 92% 自 SpaceX 上市以来，全世界第一次亲眼目睹了这家价值数万亿美元的公司的财务状况。埃隆·马斯克 (Elon Musk) 经营的公司周二公布了第二季度收益，称其收入自 6 月份以来增长了 92%。 SpaceX 的收入超出了华尔街的预期，达到 78.1 亿美元，而分析师的预测为 69.3 亿美元。尽管规模庞大，但该公司尚未盈利。该公司报告亏损 5.41 亿美元，低于去年同期的 10 亿美元亏损。继续阅读...

reflection.en: As we observe the immense financial success of a major corporation, it's a moment to reflect on the source of our ability to create wealth. Yahweh reminds us that it is He who grants the capacity to produce prosperity, inviting us to acknowledge His hand in all our endeavors. This perspective encourages gratitude and responsible stewardship of the resources...
reflection.zh: 当我们看到一家大型企业取得巨大的财务成功时，这是一个反思我们创造财富能力来源的时刻。雅伟提醒我们，是祂赐予我们创造财富的能力，邀请我们在所有的努力中都承认祂的作为。这种视角鼓励我们对所获得的资源和机会心存感恩并负责任地管理。

verse.textEn: Remember Yahweh your God, for it is he who gives you the ability to produce wealth.
verse.textZh: 你要记念雅伟你的神，因为得货财的力量是他给你的。

title.en: Mysterious elephant deaths in Kenya raise questions around pesticides
title.zh: 肯尼亚大象神秘死亡引发有关农药的疑问

summary.en: A wave of Kenyan elephant deaths has been blamed on pesticides, but experts tell the BBC they are doubtful.
summary.zh: 这是一则来自全球栏目的新闻，重点涉及和平与克制。如需完整细节，请阅读英文原始报道。

body.en:
News that the recent deaths of 15 elephants may have been caused by pesticides sprayed on tomato crops surrounding Amboseli National Park has raised concerns and questions in Kenya.

Last week, the Kenya Wildlife Service (KWS) said that some of the elephants that had died between 24 June and 24 July had shown signs of "partial paralysis" that pointed to poisoning from cyanide used in pesticides.

But conservationists have told the BBC that, perhaps, is not the full story. Farmers we have spoken to in the area were also sceptical.

"We have stayed with this wildlife for decades and have never experienced this," Daniel Nina, who represents some of the landowners in the area, told the BBC.

The tomato farms are found in the Kimana area, which is part of a corridor between Amboseli National Park and the Tsavo National Park in the south of Kenya.

It is a vast area known as the Amboseli ecosystem, which straddles the border near Tanzania where more than 2,000 elephants move along in search of food and water.

These farms thrive thanks to the streams from nearby Mount Kilimanjaro and supply markets in Kenya's capital, Nairobi, and beyond.

The chief vet of Kenya's Wildlife Service, Dr Isaac Lekolool, told us that they had found traces of cyanide in samples taken from the elephants' stomachs.

He says that they are not ruling out deliberate poisoning but it's impossible at this stage to tell what could have killed the elephants.

"It's difficult to tell because we've not seen these kind of cases before. It is almost like a one-off, and it was within a period of about a month," Lekolool said.

Their working theory is that the elephants were exposed to the toxin through pesticides sprayed on nearby tomato farms.

"It could be unintentional. Maybe people are trying to do some controls of pests on their crops, and that could have been maybe a source."

A 2024 report by Kenyan food safety initiative Route to Food found a farmer in Kimana area using an insecticide that had an "active ingredient" that was "a chemical compound of cyanide".

Wangunyu Njuguna, the author of the report, said that despite being illegal in Kenya, some toxic agrochemicals are smuggled through the border with Tanzania.

"The biggest problem is we're not enforcing similar standards in the region," Njuguna said. "There is no-one checking what I go and buy across the border, so I can just go buy anything and walk through the border and no-one stops me."

Highly hazardous substances are common on Kenyan farms and some have been linked to serious diseases.

While regulations against illegal agrochemicals exist, there's weak enforcement and little attention paid to how they can affect animals.

body.zh: 最近有消息称，安博塞利国家公园周围的番茄作物喷洒杀虫剂可能导致 15 头大象死亡，这一消息在肯尼亚引起了担忧和质疑。 上周，肯尼亚野生动物管理局 (KWS) 表示，6 月 24 日至 7 月 24 日期间死亡的一些大象出现了“部分瘫痪”的迹象，表明是因杀虫剂中使用的氰化物中毒而中毒。 但自然资源保护主义者告诉英国广播公司，这或许并不是故事的全部。我们采访过的该地区的农民也持怀疑态度。 该地区一些土地所有者的代表丹尼尔·尼娜（Daniel Nina）告诉英国广播公司（BBC）：“我们与这种野生动物相处了数十年，从未经历过这种情况。” 番茄农场位于基马纳地区，该地区是肯尼亚南部安博塞利国家公园和察沃国家公园之间走廊的一部分。 这是一个被称为安博塞利生态系统的广阔地区，横跨坦桑尼亚边境，有 2000 多头大象在此迁徙寻找食物和水。 这些农场的繁荣得益于附近乞力马扎罗山的溪流和肯尼亚首都内罗毕及其他地区的供应市场。 肯尼亚野生动物管理局首席兽医艾萨克·莱科鲁尔博士告诉我们，他们在大象胃中采集的样本中发现了氰化物的痕迹。 他说，他们不排除故意投毒的可能性，但现阶段还无法判断是什么导致了大象的死亡。 “这很难说，因为我们以前从未见过此类病例。这几乎就像是一次性的，而且发生在大约一个月的时间内，”莱科鲁尔说。 他们的工作理论是，大象是通过附近番茄农场喷洒的杀虫剂接触到毒素的。 “这可能是无意的。也许人们正在尝试对农作物上的害虫进行一些控制，这可能是一个来源。” 肯尼亚食品安全倡议“食品之路”2024 年的一份报告发现，基马纳地区的一名农民使用的杀虫剂含有“活性成分”，即“氰化物化合物”。 该报告的作者万古纽·恩朱古纳表示，尽管一些有毒农用化学品在肯尼亚是非法的，但还是通过坦桑尼亚边境走私的。 “最大的问题是我们没有在该地区执行类似的标准，”恩朱古纳说。 “没有人检查我去边境买了什么，所以我可以买任何东西然后穿过边境，没有人阻止我。” 高危险物质在肯尼亚农场很常见，其中一些物质与严重疾病有关。 尽管存在针对非法农用化学品的法规，但执行力度薄弱，而且很少关注它们对动物的影响。 然而，我们采访了几位野生动物保护主义者，他们质疑最初的……

reflection.en: This story draws attention to peace-making and restraint. Matthew 5:9 reminds us to meet sharp headlines with mercy, truth, and restraint, asking how faithful people can respond with wisdom instead of noise.
reflection.zh: 这则新闻让人想到和平与克制。Matthew 5:9提醒我们，在快速变化的新闻里，仍要以怜悯、真实与节制来回应，并学习用祷告与分辨代替情绪化判断。

title.en: 'My grandmother subjected my baby to female genital mutilation behind my back'
title.zh: “我的祖母在我背后对我的孩子进行了女性生殖器切割”

summary.en: In Colombia, where FGM is still practised by some members of an indigenous group, a landmark bill banning the practice has been enacted.
summary.zh: 这是一则来自全球栏目的新闻，重点涉及和平与克制。如需完整细节，请阅读英文原始报道。

body.en:
In what activists are calling a milestone, Colombia last week became the first country in Latin America where female genital mutilation (FGM) is now illegal.

As José Carlos Cueto reports, while the bill was passed unanimously in Colombia's Congress, it follows a long battle to eradicate the dangerous and often secretive procedure.

Carla Quiñonez's daughter was just six months old when the baby's great-grandmother subjected her to female genital mutilation (FGM) .

Quiñonez (not her real name) says when her grandmother returned the baby to her, she had a fever and was swollen and bleeding. She cried constantly.

"I confronted my grandmother, but she said it was normal and that I could not tell anyone."

The nearest health centre was a long journey away, so Quiñonez's mother, a midwife, tried to ease the baby's pain with medicinal plants. She also challenged Quiñonez's grandmother. But the older woman would not listen.

FGM involves the partial or total removal of the external female genitalia, as well as other injuries inflicted on those organs for non-medical reasons.

It can cause medical complications, including haemorrhaging and infection, as well as complications later in life with periods and during childbirth. It can also make it difficult for a woman to experience sexual pleasure.

The World Health Organization says that around the world more than 230 million girls and women alive today have been cut, predominantly in Africa.

Quiñonez, 30, has been campaigning to eradicate the practice in Colombia - where it is still practised by members of her Emberá Indigenous community.

Along with fellow activists and members of Colombia's Congress, she played a key role in the campaign which led to the ban.

She says it was only as she grew up that she realised what was secretly happening within her community.

"I remember a young cousin of mine whose birth was attended by my mother. She was born healthy, but died three days later.

"I asked my mother about it, and she told me the baby had died from 'jai', an ancestral illness."

Quiñonez now believes that girls who supposedly died from "jai" actually died from complications related to FGM.

Between 2020 and June 2026, 240 cases of FGM were recorded in Colombia. In the vast majority of instances, the girls were younger than six years old. But paediatrician Diana Ramos Mosquera says she believes this is just "the tip of the iceberg".

Working at San Jorge University Hospital in Pereira, a city in Colombia's north-west coffee-growing region, she says she's seen signs of scarring, burning and mutilation when examining girls who have come in with other medical conditions.

title.en: 'I was slut-shamed' - Indian women 'cockroach' protesters doxxed and abused

body.en:
Their videos lasted only a few seconds: lip-syncs, sarcastic reels and jokes filmed on the way to protests.

But while thousands of young people filled social media with memes and videos mocking Prime Minister Narendra Modi during one of India's biggest anti-government protest in years, many of the women behind those posts say they have paid a heavy price for speaking out.

The Cockroach Janta Party (CJP), a youth-led movement that helped force the resignation of India's education minister, relied as much on Instagram as it did on marches.

Memes, reels and viral videos became the movement's calling card, documenting everything from protest songs to the police crackdown when officers used tear gas and baton charges to stop demonstrators marching to parliament on 20 July.

Delhi police said 60 protesters and 118 police personnel were injured on the day, but the CJP said the number of injured protesters was significantly higher than the official count.

The posts reached hundreds of thousands of people, turning ordinary students into some of the movement's most recognisable faces.

Since the protests ended, police have opened criminal cases against some protesters.

But many women say another reckoning played out online. They describe rape threats, doctored images spreading on social media and strangers trawling through their photos and videos.

Some cases spilled into TV debates, police complaints and political statements. Many more unfolded quietly, as young women deleted posts, locked their accounts and stopped answering calls from unknown numbers.

The BBC spoke to four women and reviewed screenshots of abusive messages, posts and other material they shared. Their names have not been used to protect their identities.

I'm in my mid-20s. I had been posting about the protests from the beginning, but 20 July was the first time I attended one.

After the baton charge that day and the internet shutdown around the protest site, I went home and started sharing first-person accounts on Instagram.

I also helped organise food, aid and volunteers. I thought I was just helping and didn't think of it as political.

I was slut-shamed and I was attacked for questioning the prime minister's comments , external after the protest ended. [Modi said he forgave the children who had abused him, urging society to do the same rather than punish them or drag them through the courts.]

I have lost count of the number of messages I have deleted and people I have blocked. But the comments keep coming.

title.en: 'I feel like I dug my own grave': The workers caught in the AI transition
title.zh: “我感觉就像我挖了自己的坟墓”：陷入人工智能转型的工人

summary.en: AI is reshaping the Philippines' outsourcing industry, raising questions over the future of the industry.
summary.zh: 这是一则来自全球栏目的新闻，重点涉及盼望、忍耐与重建。如需完整细节，请阅读英文原始报道。

body.en:
She began writing straight out of college, freelanced for years and eventually followed a path taken by many young Filipinos: joining a multinational in the country's booming outsourcing industry.

Lisa says she never felt the need to use artificial intelligence (AI) in her work.

"I can say that I am able to do my job, I meet deadlines. In my opinion, there is no need for [AI]," she told the BBC.

Eight months into her latest role, and one month before the position was due to become permanent, she was made redundant.

In the months before, Lisa says a public relations agency had been tasked with producing AI-generated material that she and her colleagues were asked to edit. She says her skills were used to train the AI on the company writing style.

"I feel like I dug my own grave," she says. "We were the ones who trained the artificial intelligence that replaced us."

Lisa, not her real name, is one of several former outsourcing employees the BBC spoke to who asked to remain anonymous. They signed confidentiality agreements in return for severance pay, and fear that speaking publicly could hurt their chances of finding work in an industry which has a small network.

Their experiences offer an insight into a question confronting emerging economies like the Philippines: what happens when AI begins to automate the jobs that helped lift millions of people into the middle classes?

Every evening around 5pm, streams of workers wearing company lanyards spill out of high-rise offices in the district of Cubao in Manila.

It's one of several areas of the capital where multinational companies have premises – providing all sorts of outsourcing work including call centres, accounting, software development and marketing copy services for clients thousands of miles away.

For over two decades, these business districts have symbolised one of the Philippines' biggest economic success stories.

Beginning in the early 2000s, the country was promoted as an English-speaking alternative to India for what's called business process outsourcing (BPO).

Successive governments offered tax incentives, invested in infrastructure and encouraged multinational companies to set up large operations.

Global groups like Accenture, Concentrix and Teleperformance built sprawling campuses, employing hundreds of thousands of Filipinos.

Today, the outsourcing industry employs roughly 1.9 million people, and generates $40bn (£30.1bn) in revenues every year, accounting for about 10% of the Philippines' economy.

But experts say the industry is disproportionately vulnerable to the impact of AI.

body.zh: 她大学一毕业就开始写作，做了多年的自由职业者，最终走上了许多菲律宾年轻人的道路：加入该国蓬勃发展的外包行业的一家跨国公司。 丽莎说，她从未觉得有必要在工作中使用人工智能 (AI)。 “我可以说我能够完成我的工作，我能按时完成任务。在我看来，不需要 [AI]，”她告诉 BBC。 在她担任最新职务八个月后，距离该职位永久生效还有一个月，她被解雇了。 丽莎说，几个月前，一家公关机构的任务是制作人工智能生成的材料，并要求她和她的同事进行编辑。她说她的技能被用来训练人工智能了解公司的写作风格。 “我觉得我自己挖了坟墓，”她说。 “我们是训练取代我们的人工智能的人。” 丽莎（化名）是 BBC 采访的几位要求匿名的前外包员工之一。他们签署了保密协议以换取遣散费，并担心公开发言可能会损害他们在一个网络规模较小的行业找到工作的机会。 他们的经历让我们深入了解菲律宾等新兴经济体面临的一个问题：当人工智能开始实现工作自动化，帮助数百万人进入中产阶级时，会发生什么？ 每天晚上 5 点左右，戴着公司挂绳的工人从马尼拉库宝区的高层办公室涌出。 它是跨国公司在首都设有办公场所的几个地区之一，为千里之外的客户提供各种外包工作，包括呼叫中心、会计、软件开发和营销文案服务。 二十多年来，这些商业区象征着菲律宾最大的经济成功故事之一。 从 2000 年代初期开始，该国被宣传为业务流程外包 (BPO) 领域印度的英语替代品。 历届政府都提供税收优惠、投资基础设施并鼓励跨国公司开展大型业务。 埃森哲 (Accenture)、Concentrix 和 Teleperformance 等全球集团建立了庞大的园区，雇用了数十万菲律宾人。 如今，外包行业雇用了大约 190 万人，每年创造 400 亿美元（301 亿英镑）的收入，约占菲律宾经济的 10%。 但专家表示，该行业特别容易受到人工智能的影响。 国际劳工组织估计，有 1270 万菲律宾人（超过四分之一的工人）从事与生成式人工智能相关的职业，这一比例在东南部地区最高……

title.en: As allies desert FIFA boss Gianni Infantino, is there anyone ready to replace him?
title.zh: 随着盟友抛弃国际足联主帅詹尼·因凡蒂诺，有人准备好接替他了吗？

summary.en: FIFA's embattled president has found himself trapped in a controversy of his own making, and the knives are out.
summary.zh: 这是一则来自全球栏目的新闻，重点涉及和平与克制。如需完整细节，请阅读英文原始报道。

body.en:
Pressure on FIFA president Gianni Infantino has intensified, with opposition emerging both within world football's governing body and from external critics over his since-abandoned proposal to open the World Cup to private investment.

Former Arsenal manager Arsene Wenger, appointed in 2019 by Infantino as FIFA's chief of global football development, said in a statement on Tuesday that "the decision to withdraw the project was absolutely necessary and beyond question".

His remarks followed hot on the heels of an extraordinary internal email to FIFA staff, seen by the Agence France-Presse (AFP) news agency, in which secretary-general Mattias Grafstrom appeared to distance himself from Infantino on the issue.

Previously seen as close to Infantino, Grafstrom describes the fiasco surrounding the plan as "a sad and reproachable series of events".

FIFA floated the plan last Tuesday, saying it could raise up to US$4.2 billion ($5.95 billion) of private investment based on a valuation of US$20 billion ($28 billion) for a new commercial subsidiary, called the FIFA Forward Enterprise (FFE), which it proposed would handle commercial rights for events such as the World Cup and Club World Cup.

Your trusted source for staying up-to-date with the world around you. Get free daily news updates and analysis, straight to your inbox.

By Saturday, it was dead in the water, as Infantino announced he was abandoning the plan after widespread condemnation, with European governing body UEFA having threatened to boycott all FIFA competitions, including the World Cup.

Far from calming the waters or shoring up his presidency, Infantino has been swamped with criticism of his leadership style; the previously smooth path to being re-elected unopposed for a fourth and final term next March now looks rocky.

However, re-election is a problem down the road. For now, Infantion has others to confront.

Reports suggest US President Donald Trump would be "very disappointed" if Israel doesn't agree to a new peace plan for Gaza, announced last week. But how far would the US go to make that happen?

But so far the new Gaza peace deal , announced last week and meant to help end the fighting and ease the ongoing humanitarian crisis in the coastal enclave, only seems to have resulted in another standoff between the key belligerents.

However, experts point out, there are some differences between this new peace deal and previous arrangements that could be positive.

For one thing, it is much more detailed and substantive. For another, statements by Trump indicate he might be more willing to push Israel towards accepting the deal. And finally, after resisting the idea for years, this month the Gaza-based group Hamas has agreed to disarm.

It was Hamas that sent fighters into Israel on October 7, 2023, an attack that resulted in over 1,000 deaths and sparked nearly three years of an ongoing Israeli military campaign in Gaza. The Israeli military has since killed over 73,000 people there , causing a UN independent commission of inquiry to classify its behavior as a genocide.

One of the main sticking points of any peace plan for Gaza has been the sequencing of events. Israel has demanded that Hamas disarm before it withdraws its troops from Gaza. But up until last month, Hamas had refused to disarm until Israel withdrew its troops. This led to an ongoing stalemate.

Early in July, Hamas agreed to hand over power to the National Committee for the Administration of Gaza , or NCAG, a group of independent technocrats set up to govern Gaza. Later in July, the group also agreed to hand over their weapons to the NCAG.

Hamas agreeing to disarm after years of promoting armed resistance against Israel should be taken seriously, says Muhammad Shehada, a visiting fellow with the Middle East and North Africa program at the European Council of Foreign Affairs, who is originally from Gaza .

Hamas has been under pressure from negotiators from other countries like Egypt and Qatar and this could also be something of a political tactic "to expose that Israel is the party that is obstructing any progress in Gaza under [Prime Minister Benjamin] Netanyahu's government," Shehada concedes.

But, he added, "they would not have made such a major, historic concession unless their backs were totally against the wall and they fully understood that this is the only way forward."

Should Israel agree to the new peace plan, there would also be no way Hamas could renege.

title.en: South Sudan: How climate change can result in toxic water

summary.en: Years of flooding have resulted in disastrous water pollution in South Sudan's main oil region. As communities, scientists and health workers scramble for solutions, the long-term impacts of the crisis is yet to emerge.

body.en:
Years of flooding have resulted in disastrous water pollution in South Sudan's main oil region. As communities, scientists and health workers scramble for solutions, the long-term impacts of the crisis is yet to emerge.

The village of Bentiu has seen it all: Located in the north of South Sudan near the border with Sudan , the capital of Unity State used to have a population of merely several thousand people.

But war, violence and other crisis have resulted in an additional 140,000 displaced persons seeking shelter there since 2013, resulting in the establishment of a massive camp for internally displaced persons (IDPs).

Several UN bodies including the International Organization for Migration (IOM), the  UN Refugee Agency (UNHCR ) and the United Nations Children's Fund (UNICEF) are active on the ground, running what is known as the Protection of Civilians (POC) camp, which by now feels more like a permanent structure.

At a makeshift pier, children are seen playing, countless canoes bring in fish to feed scores of people at the camp, where food insecurity remains a chief concern.

Immediately, each day's yield is separated into two categories: One stock with fresh, healthy fish, and another for those believed to be contaminated. 

Simon Gatkuoth, a camp resident in his early forties, lifts a fish from a wheelbarrow, explaining that fish that are caught near the oil fields are contaminated: "When we cook them, the soup sometimes smells like penicillin," he says.

"But there is no option. We have to eat. We cannot stop eating because there is no alternative."

Viewed from the sky, the POC Camp resembles an artificial island in the midst of a region that has been transformed into what appears to be a gigantic lake. 

Here, the largely nomadic communities of South Sudan's Unity State have long adapted their lives to the seasonal floods that shape life in what is one of the world's largest wetlands known as the Sudd.

But in 2021, and unprecedented deluge of floods linked to climate change submerged farmland across the region, destroying livelihoods and killing thousands of cattle.

Just one year earlier, authorities in neighboring Uganda had issued a warning that rising levels in Lake Victoria, situated roughly 1,000 kilometers (650 miles) to the south, would require the release of large volumes of water into the White Nile river, which flows past Bentiu.

But South Sudan, one of the poorest countries, lacked the dams, flood-control systems and water-management infrastructure needed to cope with the flooding, leaving many communities highly vulnerable to flooding.

Maintained by the IOM, a simple levee is all that separates the POC Camp from the flooded plain; without constant maintenance, it would give way to the water.

title.en: What does Zambia's opposition stand without Edgar Lungu?
title.zh: 如果没有埃德加·伦古，赞比亚的反对派会怎样？

summary.en: The death of former President Edgar Lungu reshaped opposition politics in Zambia ahead of the August 13 general election. Analysts say the vote will test whether his legacy can keep opposition supporters united.

body.en:
The death of former President Edgar Lungu reshaped opposition politics in Zambia ahead of the August 13 general election. Analysts say the vote will test whether his legacy can keep opposition supporters united.

Zambia 's opposition is entering the 2026 general election without Edgar Lungu, the politician who for years united its biggest parties and inspired much of its support. Lungu, the country's former president, died in South Africa on June 5, 2025 .

Opposition parties have since been competing to inherit his political legacy while trying to convince voters they remain a credible alternative to incumbent Hakainde Hichilema's ruling United Party for National Development (UPND).

Lungu had led the now dismantled Patriotic Front (PF) party, a faction of which became part of Zambia's overall opposition Tonse Alliance in 2024. The former president had also intitially been fronted as the coalition's 2026 presidential candidate.

Political analyst Neo Simutanyi says Lungu's absence exposes an unresolved leadership question within the opposition coalition.

"He had a Plan B. He intended to back someone who would carry forward his political project, but he never had the opportunity to announce that person before he died," Simutanyi told DW.

Competing claims emerged over who should lead the Tonse Alliance emerged after Lungu's death. The coalition, now rebranded as the Tonse Pamodzi Alliance, has endorsed Brian Mundubile as its 2026 presidential candidate. He and Lungu were PF allies, while his running mate, Makebi Zulu, was Lungu's lawyer. Mundubile is widely seen as Hichilema's top challenger.

Simutanyi believes Lungu's influence nevertheless remains significant. "It is effectively a PF campaign without the PF label," he said, adding that several candidates are appealing to the same support base by presenting themselves as heirs to Lungu's legacy.

"The Edgar Lungu factor is still at play because candidates are campaigning on his legacy and many of the areas where he enjoyed strong support remain politically competitive."

Lungu's influence remains particularly visible on the Copperbelt, Zambia's mining heartland  and one of the country's most competitive electoral battlegrounds.

"Edgar Lungu's absence has left a big vacuum in the opposition, especially in the Patriotic Front. He was the one holding the party together," said Agness Tembo, a young leader from the Copperbelt.

She warned that a fragmented opposition could weaken Zambia's competitive multiparty democracy. But not all voters believe personalities will decide the election.

title.zh: 孟加拉国是否会在哈西娜后的改革中倒退？

summary.en: Two years after a student-led uprising toppled PM Sheikh Hasina, critics say Bangladesh's reform momentum is fading as political divisions deepen and key changes stall.
summary.zh: 这是一则来自全球栏目的新闻，重点涉及智慧、知识与追求真理。如需完整细节，请阅读英文原始报道。

body.en:
Two years after a student-led uprising toppled PM Sheikh Hasina, critics say Bangladesh's reform momentum is fading as political divisions deepen and key changes stall.

Just two years after a student-led uprising ended the nearly 16-year rule of Sheikh Hasina , many fear Bangladesh is slipping backward.

With Hasina, now in exile in India , planning a return in December and critics accusing the current government of failing to deliver on its promises, the country's political future is once again in doubt.

"At the end of the day, we did not see the elimination of discrimination, the creation of an inclusive society, or the new political order that was promised," Mohammad Tanzimuddin Khan, a professor of international relations at Dhaka University, told DW.

"It seems we are forgetting the very reasons behind the uprising of last July, especially those who came to power."

The protest movement began in 2018 over a controversial quota system for government jobs. In 2024, a court-backed move to reinstate parts of the system sparked fresh demonstrations that grew into a wider anti-government uprising .

In August 2024, after more than 1,000 people were killed in the unrest , then Prime Minister Hasina fled to India .

Bangladesh's interim government , which was led by Nobel Peace Prize winner Muhammad Yunus and backed by the military and key figures from the uprising, facilitated the signing of a reform roadmap. It was named the "July Charter" after the month when the uprising that toppled Hasina began. 

In a February 2026 referendum, around 70% of voters approved the charter, which proposed term limits for prime ministers, the creation of an upper house of parliament, stronger presidential powers and greater judicial independence.

The Bangladesh Nationalist Party (BNP) won a decisive majority in a general election that took place alongside the referendum .

Critics say the BNP has since failed to implement several pre-election reform commitments.

Ali Riaz, who led the interim government's Constitution Reform Commission, said there had been "time-bound commitments," including the creation of a constitutional reform council and steps to implement reforms within 180 working days.

The interim government introduced 133 ordinances as part of its reform agenda, but after the BNP came to power, it refused to adopt 20 of them — including measures concerning the National Human Rights Commission (NHRC), the Anti-Corruption Commission, enforced disappearances and referendums.

The BNP argues that constitutional and institutional changes should be enacted through proper legislative procedures in Parliament.

body.zh: 学生领导的起义推翻了总理谢赫·哈西娜两年后，批评者表示，随着政治分歧加深和关键变革停滞，孟加拉国的改革势头正在减弱。 学生领导的起义结束了谢赫·哈西娜近 16 年的统治仅仅两年后，许多人担心孟加拉国正在倒退。 目前流亡印度的哈西娜计划于 12 月回国，批评者指责现任政府未能兑现承诺，该国的政治未来再次受到质疑。 达卡大学国际关系教授穆罕默德·坦齐穆丁·汗 (Mohammad Tanzimuddin Khan) 告诉德国之声：“最终，我们没有看到消除歧视、创建包容性社会，也没有看到承诺的新政治秩序。” “我们似乎忘记了去年七月起义背后的真正原因，尤其是那些上台的人。” 抗议运动始于 2018 年，抗议政府工作配额制度颇具争议。 2024 年，一项由法院支持的恢复部分系统的举措引发了新的示威活动，并发展成为更广泛的反政府起义。 2024年8月，在骚乱中造成1000多人死亡后，时任总理哈西娜逃往印度。 孟加拉国临时政府由诺贝尔和平奖得主穆罕默德·尤努斯领导，并得到军方和起义关键人物的支持，推动了改革路线图的签署。它以推翻哈西娜的起义开始的月份命名为“七月宪章”。 在 2026 年 2 月的全民公投中，约 70% 的选民批准了该宪章，其中提出了总理任期限制、设立议会上院、更强的总统权力和更大的司法独立。 孟加拉国民族主义党（BNP）在与公投同时举行的大选中赢得了决定性多数。 批评人士称，法国国民党此后未能履行多项选举前的改革承诺。 临时政府宪法改革委员会主席阿里·里亚兹表示，已经做出了“有时限的承诺”，包括成立宪法改革委员会以及在 180 个工作日内实施改革的步骤。 临时政府出台了 133 项法令作为其改革议程的一部分，但在 BNP 上台后，拒绝通过其中 20 项法令，其中包括涉及国家人权委员会 (NHRC)、反腐败委员会、强迫失踪和公投的措施。 法国国民党认为，宪法和制度变革应通过议会适当的立法程序来实施。 法国国民党和反对派伊斯兰大会党领导的联盟在《七月宪章》上发生冲突，其中包括召开制宪会议的提议……

title.en: Spain clashes with EU countries in heated talks over migration fallout
title.zh: 西班牙与欧盟国家在移民问题上发生激烈冲突

summary.en: An estimated 60,000 people rushed into Spain's North African territory, causing major concerns throughout the European Union.
summary.zh: 估计有六万人涌入西班牙的北非领土，引发了整个欧盟的重大关切。

body.en:
Spain's interior minister headed into a tense face-off with EU counterparts on Tuesday, as the bloc sought to draw lessons from an influx of migrants into Spain's North African enclave of Ceuta in hastily arranged video talks.

The unprecedented sight of an estimated 60,000 people streaming into Ceuta from Morocco — dozens died in the attempt and almost all have since left — exposed the fault lines on migration among EU nations.

Since images first emerged of the mass arrivals, most of whom swam around a barrier separating the enclave from Morocco, the Spanish government has found itself pitted against many of its EU partners.

The bloc's interior ministers dialled in for a videoconference that could provide a chance to look for common ground — but looked equally likely to set the stage for a showdown.

While Spain moved swiftly to send migrants back from Ceuta — where it said an estimated 2,500 remained as of Monday — the government of Spanish Prime Minister Pedro Sanchez backs a more open approach to migration than most of its EU counterparts.

Countries pushing a harder line are led most vocally by Italy — whose Prime Minister Giorgia Meloni has attacked Madrid's stance, and specifically a recent push to grant legal status to undocumented migrants already in the country.

Both Italy and Denmark last week advocated suspending Spain from the Schengen free-travel area over the Ceuta crisis — a notion firmly rejected by Madrid, and which in any case is legally impossible under EU rules.

In a letter to the heads of the EU's institutions Saturday, Sanchez accused fellow EU countries of having "selfish" attitudes and called for emergency talks to work on a "common response" to such incidents.

Within hours, 22 countries led by Italy, Denmark, Germany and Hungary sent a counter-letter also demanding urgent talks, but with a different goal: to continue pressing their tough stance on immigration.

In a taste of what to expect, preparatory talks among the bloc's EU ambassadors on Monday saw Spain's envoy voice "frustration" with a perceived lack of support from fellow capitals, one EU diplomat told the Agence-France Presse (AFP) news agency.

Conversely — while all assured Madrid of their "solidarity" — some member states "are asking themselves if recent policies adopted by Spain have not sent the signal that the doors are open", added the diplomat.

The EU has significantly tightened its migration rules in recent months, including by allowing member states to send failed asylum seekers to so-called "return hubs" located outside the bloc's borders.

title.en: 'Urgent' call for military build-up in Australia's backyard amid Chinese, Russian threats
title.zh: 在中国和俄罗斯的威胁下，“紧急”呼吁在澳大利亚后院进行军事集结

summary.en: Tensions are rising in the Pacific region as distrust among key players sees one country undertake a drastic push to rearm.
summary.zh: 这是一则来自全球栏目的新闻，重点涉及和平与克制。如需完整细节，请阅读英文原始报道。

body.en:
Japan needs to boost its military with a "sense of urgency and crisis", its defence minister said on Tuesday, as a new government assessment reiterated growing risks from China, North Korea, and Russia.

Japan is already beefing up military spending and security cooperation in Asia, deploying missile launchers to outer islands, moving to acquire "counter-strike" capabilities, and easing rules on weapons exports.

But Shinjiro Koizumi said in a preface to the annual defence white paper that it was "imperative that Japan further reinforce and transform its defense capabilities with a stronger sense of urgency and crisis than ever before".

In the Asia-Pacific "not only are China and North Korea further strengthening their military capabilities, China-Russia and Russia-North Korea are also reinforcing their cooperation", he added.

The new white paper said China was "intensifying its activities" in the region around Japan, "extending beyond the so-called first island chain to the second island chain".

Japanese jets scrambled 595 times in the year to March 31, 2026, including 366 sorties against Chinese aircraft and 214 for Russian planes.

Japan decided in April to lift its self-imposed ban on weapons exports, but the white paper highlighted problems in the country's production base that could jeopardise procurement and innovation.

Koizumi also said that he and US counterpart Pete Hegseth had "exchanged candid views" on the "unwavering" US-Japan alliance, while also increasing security cooperation with the Philippines, Australia, and South Korea to realise a "a Free and Open Indo-Pacific".

"As the security environment becomes increasingly and rapidly severe, what is required now is to strengthen resilience against crises all across the entire Indo-Pacific region," Koizumi said.

"In order to do so Japan will build and expand multilayered networks among allies and like-minded countries, and enhance interconnectivity with like-minded countries and others in every area."

The link between defence and future prosperity comes as Takaichi's administration prepares a new national security strategy.

title.en: The concerning question around photos of a detained world leader
title.zh: 围绕被拘留的世界领导人照片的令人担忧的问题

summary.en: The ousted leader appeared to be in good health, her son said, but separate worries have been raised.
summary.zh: 这是一则来自全球栏目的新闻，重点涉及对脆弱群体的怜悯。如需完整细节，请阅读英文原始报道。

body.en:
Photographs of Myanmar's detained former leader Aung San Suu Kyi meeting with an aid agency have been released, a visit her son described as "extremely meaningful".

It is the first independent confirmation of her condition in years as uncertainty over the health and well-being of the 81-year-old Nobel Peace Prize winner continued to grow.

Suu Kyi has been detained since February 2021, when Myanmar's military ousted her elected civilian government in a dawn coup , plunging the impoverished Southeast Asian nation into turmoil.

The whereabouts of the former head of Myanmar's pro-Democracy party, who has a large global following, have remained largely unknown since then.

Suu Kyi's son, Kim Aris, told the Reuters news agency that the International Committee of the Red Cross (ICRC) had not been allowed to have a physician examine his mother, but said she appeared to be in good health and good spirits.

"It's the first independent proof that I've had that she's actually alive for a long time now," he said in London.

Mon Zin, an Australian-based lawyer who fled Myanmar in the 1990s with her family, told SBS News the photos offer "relief" to her supporters.

Zin is the daughter of democracy activists who fled Myanmar for Australia in 1996, where she was enrolled in Year 10.

Three decades on, she is now a lawyer and regularly contributes to analysis pieces for geopolitical publications.

She told SBS News that Suu Kyi is an "admired figure" across Asia for her decades of opposing despotism in Myanmar.

"We have always admired Aung San Suu Kyi's resilience and strength. For the people of Myanmar and many in the resistance movement, when they saw the photograph, it brought them genuine relief," she said.

One of four photographs released by the Myanmar government showed Suu Kyi in traditional Burmese dress, standing unaided and shaking hands with an ICRC representative.

Another showed the pair seated in a sparsely furnished, wood-panelled room with only two chairs and a desk.

"Timing is everything. Those who control when information is released often shape how it is interpreted and, in doing so, influence the narrative," she said.

"The junta chose to publicise a carefully managed humanitarian meeting with the ICRC, projecting humanitarian optics while continuing to deny political access to ASEAN, foreign diplomats and even her own family," Zin said.

"While many of us were relieved to see Aung San Suu Kyi alive, it is equally important to ask: Why was this information released at this particular moment?"

title.en: From petitions to memes: How students made dissent visible
title.zh: 从请愿到网络迷因：学生如何让异议显现

summary.en: Student movements throughout history, from imperial China to modern India, have consistently found new ways to express dissent and challenge established authority, adapting their methods to contemporary tools and symbols.
summary.zh: 从中国古代到当今印度，学生运动不断调整其工具和象征，以挑战权威，使异议得以显现。

body.en:
From imperial China to present-day India, student movements have repeatedly adapted the tools and symbols of their age to challenge authority.

On July 22, 2026, in rainy Mumbai, India , a casually dressed young woman stepped in front of a slow-moving police van carrying detained students. She placed her palm on the hood, forcing the vehicle to stop.

Mobile phones captured the moment from every angle. She too, raised her own phone and recorded the encounter. Within hours, the clip spread across India and beyond.

It became one of the defining visuals of the Cockroach Janta Party protests, a movement in which students demanded transparency and accountability, following leaks in India's medical entrance exams.

But the power of the moment lay not only in what she did, but in how quickly it was seen. A single gesture, a young woman confronting authority , became a symbol shared across millions of screens.

While the clip belongs to a generation raised on social media, the impulse behind it is much older.

From court petitions and revolutionary posters to photographs, umbrellas and memes, student movements have repeatedly adapted the tools and symbols available to them, turning them into vehicles for dissent.

Long before television or social media carried dissent across borders, students still found ways to make their grievances heard.

In Eastern Han China, for instance, scholars at the Imperial Academy (Taixue) aligned with reform-minded officials in opposing powerful eunuchs at court, whom many viewed as corrupt and politically overbearing.

They voiced their objections through public criticism, political networks and petitions.

In an era when political communication moved through official channels, petitions were among the established ways of bringing grievances before the throne. Written in formal language and delivered through the bureaucracy, they carried student concerns directly into the state's communication system.

In Paris in 1968, students challenged university authorities and a conservative postwar social order. As demonstrations spread across the French capital and drew in workers, one of the movement's most enduring contributions emerged from a basement workshop at the Ecole des Beaux-Arts.

The Atelier Populaire ("People's Workshop") printed thousands of posters during the protests, many of them overnight. Their bold graphics, silhouettes and slogans became the visual language of the movement. Produced collectively, many carried no individual author's name, helping transform protest into a shared public voice.

The posters and their messages could appear in dozens of places overnight, giving the protest a wide local visual presence.

Protests also became more impactful when images could be transmitted across borders.

title.en: US-China AI rivalry heats up as Chinese models gain ground

summary.en: China's AI platforms are rapidly advancing, narrowing the gap with US technology. This progress has led to renewed threats from the Trump administration, alongside accusations of intellectual property theft, raising concerns about escalating tensions between the two nations.
summary.zh: 中国的人工智能平台正迅速缩小与美国同行的差距。这一进展引发了特朗普政府新的威胁，并伴随着知识产权盗窃的指控，令人担忧两国之间的紧张关系可能升级。

body.en:
China's AI platforms are rapidly closing the gap with their US counterparts, prompting fresh threats from the Trump administration. With accusations of intellectual property theft, could tensions boil over?

In what seems like the blink of an eye,  China has gone from being up to five years behind the United States in top-tier artificial intelligence (AI) to lagging by just a few months.

While US players, including Anthropic's Claude and OpenAI's ChatGPT , have spent hundreds of billions of dollars to push the frontier of AI, China has pursued a very different path .

Faced with US curbs on high-end chips that help AI to do its most advanced thinking, Chinese tech firms have prioritized dozens of open-source AI models built on "good enough"  technology .

These platforms, including DeepSeek, Alibaba's Qwen and Xiaomi's MiMo, are now widely deployed across Chinese businesses, government services and consumer devices.

In the latest sign of the gap closing, Chinese startup Moonshot AI last week unveiled Kimi K3, a model that rivals one of the most advanced AI models — Anthropic's Claude Fable 5 — on key benchmarks.

In some tests, Kimi K3 matches or even surpasses Claude with far less computing power and at a fraction of the cost. 

Global technology specialist Alvin W. Graylin thinks Kimi K3's arrival turns high-end AI from an expensive luxury into something practical and affordable.

"For 98% of customers, the 1 to 2% difference [in knowledge] isn't worth paying 10 to 20 times more."

China's latest advance has already drawn a strong reaction from Washington, with US President Donald Trump now threatening to block US access to Chinese AI models.

Treasury Secretary Scott Bessent, meanwhile, warned earlier this week that the US could sanction Chinese models over alleged intellectual property (IP) theft.

Anthropic  and OpenAI have accused Chinese labs of using their models to train their own systems, a process known as distilling.

While distilling is a common practice by AI labs worldwide to a limited extent, the companies say their models have been bombarded with queries to harvest advanced reasoning. The White House warned in April that China was doing it on an "industrial scale."

Beijing has hit back, rejecting the accusations as baseless and calling US threats of sanctions and model bans "technological bullying" to contain China's rise.

Giulia Neaher, a research analyst at the Strategic Foresight Hub at the Washington-based Stimson Center think tank, downplayed the role of distilling in Kimi's progress.

"A great degree [of its success] is due to the talent, infrastructure and the resources that were poured into building this...
body.zh: 中国的人工智能平台正在迅速缩小与美国同行的差距，引发了特朗普政府的新威胁。随着知识产权盗窃的指控，紧张局势会升级吗？ 似乎一眨眼的功夫，中国在顶级人工智能 (AI) 领域就从落后美国五年变为仅落后几个月。 尽管包括 Anthropic 的 Claude 和 OpenAI 的 ChatGPT 在内的美国企业已经花费了数千亿美元来推动人工智能的前沿发展，但中国却走了一条截然不同的道路。 面对美国对帮助人工智能实现最先进思维的高端芯片的限制，中国科技公司优先考虑了数十种基于“足够好”技术的开源人工智能模型。 这些平台，包括 DeepSeek、阿里巴巴的 Qwen 和小米的 MiMo，现已广泛部署在中国企业、政府服务和消费设备中。 作为缩小差距的最新迹象，中国初创公司 Moonshot AI 上周推出了 Kimi K3，该模型在关键基准测试上可与最先进的人工智能模型之一——Anthropic 的 Claude Fable 5 相媲美。 在某些测试中，Kimi K3 可以与 Claude 相媲美甚至超过 Claude，但其计算能力却要低得多，而成本却只是 Claude 的一小部分。 全球技术专家 Alvin W. Graylin 认为 Kimi K3 的到来将高端人工智能从昂贵的奢侈品变成了实用且负担得起的东西。 “对于 98% 的客户来说，[知识] 1% 到 2% 的差异并不值得多付 10 到 20 倍的费用。” 中国的最新进展已经引起华盛顿的强烈反应，美国总统唐纳德·特朗普现在威胁要阻止美国使用中国的人工智能模型。 与此同时，财政部长斯科特·贝森特本周早些时候警告称，美国可能会因涉嫌盗窃知识产权而制裁中国模型。 Anthropic 和 OpenAI 指责中国实验室使用他们的模型来训练他们自己的系统，这一过程被称为蒸馏。 虽然提炼是全球人工智能实验室在一定程度上的常见做法，但这些公司表示，他们的模型已经受到查询的轰炸，以收获高级推理。白宫四月份警告说，中国正在以“工业规模”这样做。 北京方面予以反击，否认这些指控毫无根据，并称美国威胁实施制裁和示范禁令是“技术欺凌”，旨在遏制中国的崛起。 华盛顿智库史汀生中心战略远见中心的研究分析师朱莉娅·尼赫（Giulia Neaher）淡化了提炼在基米进步中的作用。 “[其成功]很大程度上归功于为建设这个项目而投入的人才、基础设施和资源......

summary.en: Gender identity, sexuality and ancestry: Here's what's new in the 2026 Census.

body.en:
The Census of Population and Housing has long tracked a changing Australia — but for more than a century, a piece of the nation's story has been missing, LGBTIQ+ Health Australia CEO Nicky Bath says.

Bath says the organisation has been calling for the addition of questions regarding sexual orientation, gender identification and expression.

"I remember in the run-up to the 2021 Census being contacted by older people who thought that they wouldn't be alive for the 2026 Census, and it was very sad for them that they wouldn't be able to participate ... in this way," she told SBS News.

The 2026 Census will now include two new questions about gender and sexual orientation.

Respondents will still be asked about their sex recorded at birth, but people over the age of 16 can also specify their gender as male, female, non-binary or another term.

Your trusted source for staying up-to-date with the world around you. Get free daily news updates and analysis, straight to your inbox.

An optional question regarding sexual orientation has been added, with answers including straight, gay or lesbian, bisexual or an open-ended response for another term.

Bath said Census data — which will be released in three phases starting from June 2027 — will inform the availability, funding and location of LGBTQI+ community and health services.

"The decision has been a long time coming ... for many people, being able to mark those boxes in the Census is really important with regards to validation and for us to be seen as important members of the community. That's a really important historical moment."

Advocates like Equality Australia say the number of people living in houseboats has been recorded in the Census for decades, but LGBTQI+ populations have not been traced.

Anna Brown, CEO of Equality Australia, said Census data collected about LGBTQI+ people would be "transformative".

"We're really looking forward to learning just how many LGBTQ+ people there are in Australia, because we know that if we aren't counted, we remain invisible in the data that shapes decisions about our lives," she told SBS News.

"Better data leads to better decisions on health, housing, education, aged care, and community services. Until now, governments have been making these decisions without a complete picture of our communities."

Brown has also called for Australians with innate variations of sex characteristics or intersex people to be counted by the Australian Bureau of Statistics (ABS).

"We will continue to advocate for its inclusion and work with the ABS ... towards recommending that this population be included," she said.

Census questions are informed by the 2020 ABS standards for sex, gender, variations in sex characteristics, and sexual orientation variables....

title.en: Australians seeing record gains and losses, as 'cracks' in housing market appear
title.zh: 随着房地产市场出现“裂缝”，澳大利亚人的收益和损失创历史新高

summary.en: Looking at property markets across Australia shows a "growing divide" in prices, experts say.
summary.zh: 这是一则来自澳洲栏目的新闻，重点涉及管家责任、供应与公共福祉。如需完整细节，请阅读英文原始报道。

body.en:
Property prices in Australia consistently reach record highs, but a "first crack in profitability" could signal a market downturn.

In the first half of 2026, 97.4 per cent of house resales resulted in a profit, slightly down from 97.5 per cent 12 months prior, according to new data from Domain released on Wednesday.

While it is a modest decline of just 0.1 per cent, it may indicate that the extended period of strong resale profitability is beginning to taper off.

Most people selling properties will still make "substantial gains", Domains chief residential economist Nicola Powell told SBS News.

However, the slight fall in national profitability suggests a slowing property market that could see prices fall in the future.

"While that shift is small, I think it is significant because what it's telling us is that resale profitability is a lagging indicator and tends to follow changes in home pricing," she explained.

"We've got some of our capital cities now going backward in price and particularly in some of our markets, we are seeing an increase in loss-making resales."

REA Group Senior Economic Analyst Megan Lieu said realestate.com.au data also revealed a drop in profitability.

In the past six months to July, 94.4 per cent of home resales made a profit, down from 94.9 per cent in the previous six months to January, she said.

But while properties are seeing larger average losses as profitability declines, some markets are soaring.

While slightly fewer properties are making a profit compared to 12 months ago, successful sellers are still enjoying record returns.

Median resale profits climbed to record levels of $458,000 for houses and $237,000 for units nationally.

Sydney posted the country’s largest resale returns, with the median house vendor achieving a profit of $739,500.

Meanwhile, Brisbane, Perth and Adelaide are increasingly standing out as the strongest markets for seller returns, with almost every resale delivering a gain.

Perth recorded the greatest proportion of profitable house resales, with 99.6 per cent of sellers making a profit on their transaction. Brisbane led the unit market, where 99.5 per cent of resales generated a positive return.

In contrast, Melbourne remained the weakest capital city market for units. More than one in four sellers sold for less than their original purchase price, while Melbourne also recorded one of the highest shares of loss-making house resales, alongside Canberra.

Surprisingly, some areas saw both record profitability gains and losses over the year.

title.en: Police probing 'pro-Palestinian motives' in terror investigation into arson attack

body.en:
An arson attack on a Melbourne defence firm is now being investigated as an act of terrorism, with counter-terror police alleging the offenders had pro-Palestinian motives.

On 5 July, machining manufacturer Lovitt Technologies was attacked in the early hours of the morning by arsonists who set three vehicles alight and graffitied a building.

The Victorian Joint Counter Terrorism team (JCTT), spanning Australian Federal Police (AFP), Victoria Police and ASIO, has released images of the alleged vandals, probing whether "far-left activists with anarchist and revolutionary ideologies" orchestrated the incident.

The group is alleged to have targeted the company because of its links with the defence force supply chain, claiming responsibility in an online video and advising on how to carry out similar attacks.

The JCTT said the alleged offenders "outlined a number of grievances in support of Palestine" and were accused of targeting the company because they believed it was part of a broader Australian Defence Force supply chain.

Images released by the AFP show a suspect wearing all black clothing, standing in front of a Palestinian flag. Aboriginal and Torres Strait Islander flags are also displayed in the foreground.

In 2023, Lovitt secured a $1.5 million grant to continue work on the global Joint Strike Fighter program — a US-led F35 fighter jet construction program of which Israel is a key recipient.

The JCCT has confirmed to SBS News that the terror investigation, known as Operation Braehead, is the first to specifically target pro-Palestinian activism in Australia since the October 7 attacks. The charges carry a life sentence as a maximum penalty.

"We cannot overstate the seriousness of this criminality and the AFP, together with our partners, will not tolerate acts of terror motivated by extremist ideologies aiming to cause fear and anguish in our community," AFP detective superintendent Anthony Hall said in a statement.

"At any time, we could be knocking on the door of the accused group. We know this is making some in the group anxious — and it should, because we are determined to bring them before the courts."

Victoria Police detective acting superintendent Anthony Wheatfill said companies and employees "have the right to go about their daily business safely and securely."

"That anyone would use such violent and dangerous methods to express a political or social viewpoint is unacceptable."

body.en:
It was once a dream of many: work hard and retire in your 60s. Now, more Australians are employed into their 70s, 80s and even 90s. Insight meets those still working by choice, those who can't afford to stop, and asks what happens when you keep working later in life? Watch Insight episode Working Later in Life on SBS On Demand.

Working Later In Life episode • Insight • News And Current Affairs • 52m I was devastated when I turned 65.

I was working as an interpreter for a government telephone interpreter service, and at the time, 65 was the compulsory retirement age from the public service.

My body and mind felt young — I was perfectly capable of work — and people needed my help. I couldn't believe that an arbitrary age meant I had to stop working full-time.

I went to the union and to a solicitor, but they couldn't help me, so I had to retire — kicking and screaming on my way out. But I found a workaround: freelance work.

I'm now 94 years old, interpreting and translating in both the private and public sectors (including Centrelink), and have no plans to retire soon.

Becoming an interpreter was always a natural progression for me; I speak a few languages, and I love dealing with people.

I was born and raised for the first 12 years of my life in Hungary. But in 1945, near the end of World War Two, my parents and I fled as refugees to Germany after the Soviet Red Army invaded and occupied our country.

I already knew Hungarian, but I learnt German, English, Latin and French through my six years of schooling in Germany, which have been very helpful to know.

I arrived in Melbourne with my family in January 1951, after 65 days of travel, as displaced persons from the war.

I was 18 years old and still remember feeling a heat I had never experienced in my life when we were taken to Bonegilla, an ex-army camp near Albury in northern Victoria that was then used as a camp to process post-war European migrants.

Because the camp was full, we were put in an army tent — and that is how I started my life in Australia.

It wasn't until the late 1950s, when I was in my late 20s, a mother and working an admin role, that my interpreting career began.

The 1956 Hungarian Revolution brought a wave of Hungarian migrants to Australia in the years that followed. But there was no community interpreter service here at the time, and people needed help.

So I stepped forward as an interpreter. I believe it's important to be understood as a person — to say what you want to say and be able to express yourself. And if you don't speak the language of a place, that's very hard to do.

body.en:
WARNING: Aboriginal and Torres Strait Islander readers are advised that this story includes the name of an Indigenous person who has passed away.

When former AFL player for Essendon, Shawn Lewfatt, signed up as an Aboriginal Community Police Officer in Darwin in 1998, he was excited by the chance to work with his own people "for the better".

Now, he says, he would "never encourage" his adult children to join the Northern Territory Police Force (NTPF).

"My aim is that hopefully one day I can turn to young people and encourage them to join," he told SBS News.

Lewfatt is part of a landmark class action filed in the Federal Court against the NTPF seeking compensation for allegations of racial discrimination and racial vilification while serving as Aboriginal Community Police Officers (ACPOS) going back almost three decades.

"Our clients allege they were underpaid, provided fewer opportunities for career advancement and subjected to persistent racist conduct while serving communities across the NT," Seb O'Meara of Gordon Legal, who is representing the ACPOs in the class action, told SBS News.

The class action, run on behalf of all present and former Aboriginal police officers in the NT Police, seeks to speed up reform following the 2019 police shooting of Kumanjayi Walker and the subsequent inquest, which shone the spotlight on systemic racism within the NT Police Force.

A spokesperson for the NTPF told SBS News they were aware of ongoing legal proceedings, and it would be inappropriate to comment further.

Despite growing up in Darwin, Lewfatt told SBS News that when he walked through the doors of the police station, he felt like a "foreigner in my hometown".

"I felt immediately weird in the way they would speak about Aboriginal people, and it became clear to me that it was the norm."

Lewfett, who remains on the Force on leave, alleged he witnessed "unlawful assaults on Indigenous people", including one incident involving a non-Aboriginal police officer urinating into a wine cask belonging to an Aboriginal member of the public who had stashed it in a public toilet.

Lewfatt said that racism in the force is embedded in the culture, rather than in individuals.

"It's the systematic racism where there are a lot of good people who may not be racist but do not call out racism either when they come across it."

body.en:
The egg industry has so far remained unaffected by the H5N1 avian influenza (bird flu) outbreak; however, precautionary measures to limit the spread of the virus could drastically reduce free-range egg production.

The recent H5N1 outbreak in South Australia has sparked widespread concern for the health and safety of not only the wild bird population but also commercial farming.

Australian Eggs managing director Rowan McMonnies said the industry is "facing up to a riskier operating environment for the foreseeable future".

"Transmission between Australian wildlife indicates H5 avian influenza is established and is here to stay in the medium term," he said.

Your trusted source for staying up-to-date with the world around you. Get free daily news updates and analysis, straight to your inbox.

McMonnies said whilst eradication "seems unlikely", the industry has been preparing for an outbreak of this type for several years.

"Important actions are being taken to address the risks. Strict biosecurity is being maintained with enhanced measures to deter wild birds and limit crossover into egg farms," he said.

"The industry has also worked closely with authorities to improve response processes based on overseas learnings so that where farms are impacted, they can bounce back faster, limiting any impact on egg supply."

Since 2018, the Australian Competition and Consumer Commission (ACCC) has enforced the standard that for an egg product to be considered free range it must be laid by hens that have meaningful and regular access to outdoor range during daylight, are able to roam and forage in a stocking density of 10,000 hens or less per hectare, and that the density be displayed on produced products.

However, as of July, the ACCC confirmed it won’t take enforcement action for breaches of free-range egg labelling standards due to farms choosing to house birds inside for biosecurity reasons.

Limiting free-range environments is a biosecurity measure many chicken farms are using.

"The advice is to confine birds to sheds," microbiologist and food safety expert Associate Professor Julian Cox told SBS News.

"Birds of free-ranging pick up the virus and interact — potentially spreading it to noncommercial species .... or wild birds in the vicinity could bring it into commercial poultry that are free-ranging," he explained.

Cox said it’s a measure anyone who owns and cares for poultry should consider.

"If you've got some kind of coop, lock them in the coop. It’s for their own good."

reflection.zh: 关于散养鸡蛋的新闻突显了人类在照管受造物方面所肩负的复杂责任。虽然我们常寻求理想条件，但智慧有时要求我们做出艰难的调整，以保护我们所看管之物的福祉，即便这意味着在充满挑战的环境中重新评估何为‘好’，正如雅伟神将人安置在伊甸园中，使其耕作并看守。

verse.textEn: Yahweh God took the man and put him in the Garden of Eden to work it and take care of it.
